title: A scripted walk can open a menu in the panel and drag a tile out of it
goal: The automated walks that prove features work can only drive the picture. They cannot open a menu inside the right hand panel, and they cannot drag anything out of it. That is where a growing share of the app now lives, so five separate pieces of work in one day had to claim something was right without a picture of it. Give the walks those two moves.
notes: Design review finding, 2026-09-03: five audits in one day admit the same blind spot. queue/audits/2026-09-03-knob-naming.json and 2026-09-03-component-choice-one-step.json (a menu inside the dock cannot be opened by a walk, so its rows are covered by a test rather than a picture), 2026-09-03-layers-tree.json (the harness drives the canvas, not the inspector, and cannot synthesise a panel drag, so the drop indicator picture came from a one-off), 2026-09-03-library.json (dragging a tile and double clicking a tile are both hand paths). 2026-09-03-readable-component-tiles.json also reports that focusing the Library search field hangs the app in a walk; the name field work later the same day (commit b4e804d) touched that box, so check whether it still hangs before assuming it does. The harness is Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PlaytestHarness.swift with its script model in PhotonzCore (PlaytestScript); actions are added in pairs, a pure step in the model and a driver in the harness.
acceptance: A walk can open a menu inside the right hand panel and photograph its rows
A walk can drag a tile from the Library onto the picture and the layer lands where it was dropped
A walk can drag a row in the layers list onto another row and photograph the line that says what will happen
One existing feature that could only be proved by a test is re-proved by a walk with a picture
Focusing the Library search box in a walk does not hang the app
